title: Let a running cyclotron take newly accepted primed examples
description:
## Why
The hosted priming demo (paste a URL, label it publish or reject with an optional explanation, save, and see the classifier use it) cannot work on a running newsroom: an embedded store only accepts priming when it is first created, and refuses new examples on reopen.

## What
- `Cyclotron.add_priming_examples(examples, *, added_by)` adds accepted, human-labeled examples to an existing store, with no model call.
- Each output that gains examples appends them to its fixed example list as a new version (`lastChange.summary`: "Added N primed example(s) to the example list."). Unreviewed decisions are decided again by that version.
- The learned head no longer matches the changed context, so the new version starts unfitted until the next learning pass.
- Idempotent for identical examples; refuses changed content for a known identity, items already decided, unknown labels, and a blank `added_by`.
- `priming_additions()` records who added which examples and when. Additions are applied once per output, so an example the optimizer later swaps out is not put back on reopen; an interrupted addition completes on reopen.
- Reopening with the creation-time `priming_examples` still works after additions.

```gherkin
Feature: Priming a running cyclotron
  Scenario: A saved example reaches the next decision
    Given a running cyclotron with no primed examples
    When an editor adds a primed example labeled "exclude" with an explanation
    Then the cyclotron is at version 2 with 1 primed example
    And the next decision request carries that example in its example list
